guide.summary: Old Montreal landmarks, Sherbrooke Street museums, parks and public markets, with bagels, brunch, dinners and cocktail bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Mondays are a weak museum day: Pointe-à-Callière lists no Monday hours, the McCord Stewart Museum is closed Mondays, and the Marguerite-Bourgeoys Museum closes Mondays from October 16 to May 14.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Pointe-à-Callière and the McCord Stewart Museum have no Monday opening, and Beauty's Luncheonette is closed Tuesdays. Le Club Chasse et Pêche and Le Vin Papillon serve dinner Tuesday to Saturday only.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: The Montreal Museum of Fine Arts requires reservations for Chiharu Shiota: The Soul Trembles (to February 14, 2027) except for members. Pointe-à-Callière sells tickets online or at the counter until 60 minutes before closing.

toolkit.label: Walk-in policy
toolkit.copy: Le Mal Nécessaire takes no reservations after 8 p.m. on Fridays and Saturdays and seats first come, first served. Bar Henrietta takes no reservations and opens daily at 4 p.m.

toolkit.label: Rules and prices
toolkit.copy: Pointe-à-Callière's concession rates require a valid ID, adults pay $30 and children under 5 enter free. The McCord Stewart Museum offers free admission on Wednesdays from 5 p.m.

guide.dek: Plan museum days for Tuesday to Sunday, book the Shiota exhibition ahead, and save the walk-in cocktail bars for early evening.
intro: Start in Old Montreal, where Notre-Dame Basilica at 110 Notre-Dame Street West lists a Choral Christmas Concert by the Metropolitan Orchestra on December 8, 2026, with tickets through TicketPro. A short walk away, Pointe-à-Callière at 350 Place Royale opens Tuesday to Sunday and runs Heroes of Greece. The Age of Troy until March 7, 2027; tickets are sold until 60 minutes before closing. Château Ramezay on Notre-Dame Street East and the Marguerite-Bourgeoys Museum on rue Saint-Paul Est add more history, though the latter closes on Mondays from October 16 to May 14.

Uptown, the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts at 1380 Sherbrooke Street West shows Chiharu Shiota: The Soul Trembles through February 14, 2027, and you need a reservation for it unless you are a member. Anne Kahane: Structures opens there on November 19, 2026. The McCord Stewart Museum at 690 Sherbrooke West is closed Mondays, stays open until 9 p.m. on Wednesdays with free admission from 5 p.m., and is renovating its ground floor. Saint Joseph's Oratory on Queen Mary Road is open from 6:30 a.m. to 9 p.m.

For open space, the city lists Mount Royal Park and Parc La Fontaine as open from 6 a.m. to midnight every day, and Mount Royal is marking its 150th anniversary with activities running from June 2026 to May 2027. The city's public markets make easy lunches: Jean-Talon opens at 8 a.m. Monday to Saturday, Atwater opens at 9 a.m., and Maisonneuve holds children's culinary workshops on November 14, 2026. Down by the river, La Grande Roue de Montréal turns from 10 a.m. to 11 p.m., with tickets sold through Fever.

For food, Fairmount Bagel bakes at 74 Fairmount West, Beauty's Luncheonette serves from 8 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. and closes Tuesdays, and Crew Collective & Café serves brunch daily from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. in Old Montreal. L'Express on Saint-Denis is open seven days from 11:30 a.m. to 1 a.m., while Le Club Chasse et Pêche and Le Vin Papillon open for dinner Tuesday to Saturday. For drinks, Le Mal Nécessaire stops taking reservations after 8 p.m. on Fridays and Saturdays, and Bar Henrietta on Laurier West takes none.
summaryCards: Pair Notre-Dame Basilica and Pointe-à-Callière in Old Montreal, then book the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts for the Chiharu Shiota exhibition.
Pick up bagels at Fairmount Bagel or brunch at Crew Collective & Café, then walk Mount Royal Park, open from 6 a.m.
Check closing days first: Pointe-à-Callière and the McCord Stewart Museum have no Monday opening and Beauty's closes Tuesdays.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Several operator sites could not be read: St-Viateur Bagel, Schwartz's, Olive et Gourmando, Joe Beef, Café Olimpico, Hof Kelsten and Fous Desserts returned HTTP 429, the Musée d'art contemporain returned 403, Larrys had an expired certificate and Boulangerie Guillaume failed DNS lookup. Espace pour la vie pages (Botanical Garden, Biodôme) redirect to a calendar with no address. Hours were not published on the pages read for Notre-Dame Basilica, Château Ramezay, the Montreal Science Centre and Fairmount Bagel, and several restaurants, cafés and bars show only hours or booking links without dated 2026 text, so they are marked medium confidence.
